purpose: Evaluate and update policy status lifecycle for TFG Personal Lines Policy Processing by reading validated policy master records, applying date-based status transition rules, and producing status-updated policy extracts with error reporting for date validation failures.
high_level_narrative: The program initiates by retrieving the system current date and validating it as a legitimate calendar date. It then opens three sequential files: POLICY-IN for input policy records, POLICY-OUT for updated policy output, and ERROR-OUT for date validation exceptions. The main processing loop reads each policy record from POLICY-IN, validates the effective date and expiry date as valid calendar dates, and ensures expiry date is not before effective date. If any validation fails, an error record with specific error code (S001, S002, S003) is written to ERROR-OUT. For valid records, the program determines the new policy status: preserves 'CN' (Cancelled) if already cancelled; otherwise assigns 'PN' (Pending) if current date is before effective date, 'AC' (Active) if current date falls on or between effective and expiry dates, or 'EX' (Expired) if current date exceeds expiry date. When the status changes, the PO-UPDATE-DT field is set to the current system date. The updated policy record is written to POLICY-OUT. Counters track reads, writes, status changes, and each status category. Upon end-of-file, all files are closed and processing statistics are displayed.
business_domain: Policy Administration / Policy Lifecycle Management in Personal Lines Insurance
inputs: POLICY-IN (sequential file, 77-char records containing policy master data)
System current date via FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE
outputs: POLICY-OUT (sequential file, 77-char records with updated policy status)
ERROR-OUT (sequential file, 70-char records for date validation exceptions)
Console display of processing statistics (reads, writes, changes, status counts, rejects, I/O errors)
key_transformations: Calendar date validation for effective date, expiry date, and system date including leap year calculation
Policy status determination based on date comparison rules
Record copy from input to output with conditional status field update
Update timestamp (PO-UPDATE-DT) refresh when policy status changes
Error record construction with policy number, error code, and descriptive message
key_dependencies: No external copybooks or copy members referenced
business_rules: If existing policy status = 'CN' (Cancelled), preserve 'CN' regardless of dates
If current date < effective date => status = 'PN' (Pending)
If current date <= expiry date => status = 'AC' (Active)
If current date > expiry date => status = 'EX' (Expired)
Effective date must be a valid calendar date (validated via VALIDATE-CALENDAR-DATE)
Expiry date must be a valid calendar date (validated via VALIDATE-CALENDAR-DATE)
Expiry date must be greater than or equal to effective date
System current date must be a valid calendar date
Policy status change triggers update of PO-UPDATE-DT to current system date
Leap year calculation: year divisible by 400, or divisible by 4 but not by 100
